subject: TTL tailoring & pilot economics — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@carepath.com>, Samir Rao <samir@carepath.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: TTL tailoring & pilot economics — next steps

Hi Olivia / Samir — great to meet today, thanks for walking through the CarePath use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone has the same view:

Summary from call:
- Primary ask: 0-retention for any fields flagged as PII (names, SSNs, patient IDs) when routed to our hosted inference.
- Secondary: reduce KV cache retention for non-PII conversational state to a short window (they suggested 24–72 hours) for troubleshooting only.
- Residency: Platform will be served from US regions initially; CarePath asked for an EU residency option for an eventual go-live.
- Audit evidence: they want SOC2 evidence and a short operational checklist for the pilot.

Our proposal (pilot):
- Pilot scope: 30-day technical pilot for one product flow (appointment triage) on a dedicated ephemeral routing policy.
- Retention controls: Enable our ephemeral mode for PII (zero-persistence) and a configurable KV TTL of 48 hours for non-PII during pilot.
- Logging: Minimal operational logs retained for 7 days for debugging; we redact conversational PII from logs via pipeline filters.
- Security evidence: attach SOC2 snapshot and a proposed pilot scope document (attached).
- Commercials: pilot credit for usage up to 50k tokens + standard per-token pricing for any overage.

Open asks for CarePath (need answers to move forward):
1) Can you confirm the exact fields you consider PII (we put a preliminary list in the attached scope)?
2) Are you OK with 48-hour KV TTL during pilot (we can trial 24h but it impacts troubleshooting)?
3) Any legal redlines that would block a 0-retention operational mode?
4) Who in your security team should receive the SOC2 packet and the pilot checklist?

Next steps:
- If you confirm fields + KV TTL, we will send a pilot SOW + updated security checklist for signature (DocuSign link included).
- Internal: loop in legal and Security for a quick review of the concession language (I cc'd Marissa and Ben).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with an updated SOW once we get the field list.

—Jordan

Thanks Jordan — recap looks right. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- PII fields: primary list is patient_name, patient_dob, patient_ssn, patient_id, insurance_number. We can share an exported schema by EOD.
- KV TTL: security prefers 24 hours for KV, but product would like 48 hours for debugging; we may accept 48h during the pilot if we can see stricter redaction of any PII in logs.
- Residency: EU option is not required for pilot, but will be a must for our 2028 roadmap.
- SOC2 packet: please send to sec-eval@carepath.com (Samir is looping them in separately).

One more ask: legal wants to see the exact language you intend for the zero-persistence concession (they asked for a sample SOW clause). Can your team draft a clause we can review?

Olivia

Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: suggested SOW clause + pilot economics (internal)

Internal notes for the pilot negotiation — copied to thread when we have a draft: 

- SOW clause suggestion (high level): 
  "Redwood will not persist fields classified as PII in persistent storage when requests are routed via the 'ephemeral' routing policy. Ephemeral routing ensures no conversation inputs or outputs flagged as PII are written to durable object storage. Operational logs necessary for service health and debugging will be retained for a maximum of 7 days; such logs will be subject to redaction rules agreed in Schedule A."

- KV TTL recommendation: offer 48h as default for pilot with option for 24h for a production-tier contractual addendum. Notes: 24h will increase time-to-triage (higher support friction).
- Evidence pack: include SOC2 snapshot + architecture diagram showing in-memory-only KV option and our redaction pipeline.
- Commercials: we can absorb one pilot month of usage up to 50k tokens; beyond that, standard hosted pricing. Keep any legacy discounts off the table for pilot.

Suggested internal next steps: Marissa to run the draft clause by legal; Jordan to send the draft clause + SOW to Olivia; I’ll prepare the technical appendix and redaction checklist.

Ben

Head, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Olivia / Samir — thanks for the fast replies and the field list preview. Next steps and immediate asks below so we can get the SOW out today: 

1) Jordan: drafting a short 0-persistence SOW clause (see Ben's suggested language attached) and will send to you for redline. Expect that in the next 2 hours.
2) CarePath: if you can confirm whether you can accept 48h KV TTL for the pilot (we will call out 24h as a stricter production option), that lets us finalize the pilot config.
3) Samir: please confirm the security contact (sec-eval@carepath.com) is correct and whether we should push the SOC2 packet to them directly or via your procurement thread.
4) Legal: Marissa is reviewing the draft clause; any material blocking language (e.g., absolute indemnities tied to data retention) will slow the pilot. If you have procurement redlines now, please share.

I’ll attach the SOW and the redaction checklist once Marissa gives the green light. Looking forward to moving this to a short technical pilot — Jordan will be the pilot owner from our side.
